pathways.climate_pressure: Long dry spells and reliance on rainwater.
pathways.documented_impact: Inadequate household storage increases dependence on shared water distribution.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access and competition at constrained water points.
pathways.possible_consequence: NAP reports water theft/disputes and community stress, without incidence or causal estimates.
alternative_explanations: Storage investment, power reliability, distribution rules and household resources also shape shortages and grievances.
pathways.uncertainty: Government NAP synthesis citing CIVRA 2024, not a new event inventory or proof of climate-caused armed violence. No island-specific dispute claim.
resilience_factors: Storage, inclusive allocation and conflict-sensitive assistance are identified responses; effects are unevaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Tuvalu's NAP links dry spells and insufficient storage with shared-water disputes; local frequency and distribution remain unknown.

gaps: Main corrected physical-versus-printed spread pagination in the six-page 2022 profile. Its findings expressly remain provisional.

NAP synthesis links long dry spells and storage deficits with distribution-point disputes, but does not quantify frequency or assign events to individual islands. Migration and assistance risks remain conditional.

executive_assessment.text: The NAP distinguishes coastal-flood scenarios for Funafuti, Nui, Nukufetau and Vaitupu and describes storage-related water tensions without incident rates.
Funafuti land/service pressure and conditional assistance grievances add FCV depth; named island grants and training are reported outputs, not independent resilience or peace effects.
